title: delurio needs of a flow (needs.yaml)
description: What must exist for a flow's users, in delurio-graph/0 (SPEC.md §13): a closed list beside the flow's flow.yaml, each need with the evidence that it exists, or `missing` and why it does not yet. A need that is missing is a gap of the product, listed in its needs.gaps.yaml.

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A needs.yaml is `needs`.

id.description: The id of the flow beside this file, whose needs these are.

title.description: The list in plain words, for people.

summary.description: Where the needs come from and what they cover, in a few plain sentences.

status.description: `proposed`: written, nobody has approved it. `approved`: the owner reviewed and accepted the list. A list is written from what the flow's users need, never read from the code, so it is never `captured`.

needs.description: The needs, in the order people read them. Each id comes once.

formatVersion.description: The format and its version. Every graph file starts with it.

need.description: One thing that must exist for the flow's users. A need without `missing` is met, and names evidence outside the graph (a source, a test, a scenario or a setting); a need with `missing` is a gap, and may name what exists of it so far.
What must exist, in a sentence of the graph's language, from the users' side: what they can do or what they are told.
examples: The owner of an archived note restores it from the note's own page, and it is active again.

evidence.description: What shows that the need exists: the code, a test, a scenario that walks it, the states and nodes it is drawn as, a setting a deployment gives. Every piece must resolve.

missing.description: That the need does not exist yet, and why or where that is tracked: words, an issue, a finding's id. Its flow and id must then be in the product's needs.gaps.yaml.
examples: archived notes are not erased yet; the second phase erases them

note.description: The author's own words. No tool reads them.

needId.description: A need's id in its flow: kebab-case. The gaps name it so.

path.description: A path relative to the application's repository root (SPEC.md §9).

evidence.description: One piece of evidence, of one kind: `source`, `test`, `scenario`, `state`, `node` or `setting`.

source.description: The code that makes the need true: `<path>:<line>`, or a bare `<path>` for a whole file, relative to the application's repository root (SPEC.md §9). The file must exist and have that line.

test.description: A test of the need: its file, relative to the application's repository root. The file must exist.

name.description: With `source`: a name the file holds, such as the function that does it. With `test`: the test's name as it is written, in quotes or as a test function's name. The file must hold it, not as a part of a longer word.

scenario.description: A scenario of a binding (SPEC.md §7) that walks the need on the app. The binding is the flow's own binding.yaml, or the one `binding` names; it binds this flow and has the scenario, its `extends` included.

binding.description: With `scenario`: the binding that has it, relative to the application's repository root, when it is not the flow's own binding.yaml.

state.description: A state of the flow the need is drawn as. Where only missing needs name it, a tool that walks the flow on the app leaves it out.

node.description: A node of the flow's screens (ui.yaml) the need is drawn as. Where only missing needs name it, a tool that walks the flow on the app leaves it out.

setting.description: An environment variable a deployment sets for the need. The file `in` names sets it on a line that is not commented out.

in.description: With `setting`: the file that tells a deployment what to set, relative to the application's repository root: a dotenv file such as .env.example, or a Compose file.
